apExam.body: Most of the AP Seminar score comes from an individual research report, an individual presentation, and a team project, not a single sit-down test.

facts.label: Individual research report
facts.text: A written argument using multiple sources, about 35% of the score.

facts.label: Individual multimedia presentation
facts.text: A spoken argument with questioning, about 20% of the score.

facts.label: Team project and presentation
facts.text: A collaborative argument and presentation, about 20% of the score.

facts.label: End-of-course exam
facts.text: A 2-hour written exam: short-answer analysis of a source set, then an essay building and supporting an argument. About 25% of the score.

heroBody: AP Cybersecurity is a newer AP Career Kickstart course about how systems are attacked and defended. Practice reasoning through protocols and attacks with sequence diagrams on screen, and get feedback on your explanations.
phoneAlt: Lune Synth question with a sequence diagram of a TCP handshake (SYN, then SYN-ACK, then an unknown third message), asking which message a SYN flood withholds and why it exhausts the server.
phoneLabel: AP Cybersecurity · TCP handshake and SYN flood
problemHeadline: Naming an attack is not the same as explaining it.
problemBody: Security questions reward the mechanism: which message an attacker withholds, which resource runs out, which control breaks the chain. Vocabulary lists do not build that reasoning.
contrastAfter: Explain the mechanism and the defense

benefits.title: Reason through it
benefits.body: Work from a protocol diagram to what an attacker changes and why it matters.

benefits.title: Get precise feedback
benefits.body: Feedback points to the missing link between the attack and its effect.

benefits.title: Practice the next one
benefits.body: Short sets on related attacks and defenses.

exampleHeadline: Connect the missing message to the exhausted resource.
attempt: A SYN flood sends a lot of traffic.
observation: Volume is part of it, but the mechanism is half-open connections waiting for a final ACK that never comes.
hint: What does the server keep in memory while it waits?
nextPractice: Three protocol diagrams asking which step an attack abuses and which defense breaks it.
